findings.title: Organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition)
findings.body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which stores the slug when billing is off. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips that. On deployments without team billing the organization is now created with no slug, so org routing by slug breaks. The PR description does not mention this change, and it is unrelated to the calendar work. Restore `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, or revert the line if the flip was intended, and say so in the PR.
findings.originReason: The diff changed `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`.

verification.reason: Base spread `{ slug }` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. Head spreads it only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, so the condition is flipped. Self-hosted deployments without billing now create orgs without a slug.

findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences a possibly undefined destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (null or []). The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without `?.`. The old code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. When `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and there is no destination calendar, `create()` throws a TypeError before any calendar is written. handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067). Fix: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

verification.reason: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or [], the destructuring gives `undefined`. When the location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is then read without optional chaining and throws a TypeError.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent/updateEvent fallback compares externalId to itself and yields undefined
findings.body: In deleteEvent, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. The predicate compares to null/undefined/"", so the result is effectively undefined. The old fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. At line 322, `calendarId` then becomes "primary", and the 404 is resolved silently at line 335. A cancelled booking therefore leaves its event on the user's selected calendar, with no error shown. The same pattern is at line 256 in updateEvent, where calendarId becomes undefined and Google rejects the update. Restore the previous fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, or a credential-matched lookup if you want the multi-destination case handled) in both places.

verification.reason: The fallback predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never matches a real calendar. Delete then falls back to "primary", and the 404 is resolved silently. Update passes calendarId undefined. Previously both used `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`.

findings.title: Legacy destination calendars (no credentialId) are ignored by Google createEvent
findings.body: Google now picks the calendar with `cal.credentialId === credentialId` (lines 147-149). Destinations without a credentialId are routed by EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents' else branch (packages/core/EventManager.ts:375-383), which calls `createEvent(c, event)` with no externalId. For those, the find returns nothing and the event goes to "primary". The old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which was the user's chosen calendar. CalendarManager.createEvent also receives `externalId` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:221) and drops it: it passes only `credential.id` at line 236. Pass the destination externalId through to the calendar service, or match on credentialId with a fallback to the destination that has none.

verification.reason: The else branch of createAllCalendarEvents calls `createEvent(c, event)` for destinations that have no credentialId. Google's createEvent matches on `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, which fails for those destinations, so the event goes to "primary" instead of the chosen externalId. CalendarManager also drops its `externalId` parameter.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar, whatever credential is inserting
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` (line 73) is used for the URL at lines 75-76 for every call, but EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination with that destination's credential (packages/core/EventManager.ts:370). With collective events, the array holds other hosts' destinations, so a team member's Outlook credential posts to the organizer's calendar id. That request returns 404, and CalendarManager.createEvent swallows 404s with no log (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:243-245). The member's event is silently not created. Lark has the same `[0]` selection (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129 and 164-165), which fails loudly rather than silently. Select the destination that matches the credential, as Google does, or pass the destination externalId into createEvent.

verification.reason: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination's externalId, but EventManager now calls it once per destination with that destination's credential. A team member's credential therefore posts to the organizer's calendar id. One detail is wrong: handleErrorsJson throws `Error(statusText)` with no `.code`, so CalendarManager logs the failure instead of swallowing it as a 404. The failure is not fully silent, but the event is still not created.

findings.title: Meet-link patch uses a different calendarId from the insert
findings.body: The insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` (line 154), but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` (line 168). When no destination matches the credential, the insert lands in primary and the patch sends an undefined calendarId. The patch has no callback, so its failure is an unhandled promise rejection and the description with the hangout link is never written. Use the same resolved calendar id in both calls.

verification.reason: The insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the patch passes `selectedCalendar` as is, which can be undefined when no destination matches the credential. The patch has no callback or catch, so a rejection goes unhandled and the hangout link description is never written.

findings.title: Each legacy destination calendar re-creates the event on every organizer credential of that type
findings.body: In the `else` branch (no destination credentialId), each destination of a matching integration calls `createEvent(c, event)` for every credential in `this.calendarCredentials` of that type (lines 376-381). With a collective event that has two or more legacy destinations of one integration, the organizer's calendar receives duplicate events. Each call goes to the same calendar because the Google service ignores the destination externalId (see the Google createEvent finding). This assumes `calendarCredentials` holds only the organizer's credentials. I confirmed that the constructor filters the list passed in (line 85) but did not read the caller that passes it. Confirm the caller, then dedupe the destinations or limit the else branch to a single credential.

verification.reason: For each destination without a credentialId, the else branch creates the event on every organizer credential of that integration type. The EventManager is built from organizerUser's credentials (handleNewBooking.ts:1254, 2002). Several legacy collective destinations of the same integration therefore produce duplicate events on the organizer's calendars.

findings.title: Empty dynamic user list is reported as 500, not 400
findings.body: The new `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is a plain Error inside the try block. The catch at lines 757-761 rethrows only HttpError and Prisma errors as 400, so this error becomes `HttpError 500 "Unable to load users"`. A client sending an empty dynamicUserList gets a server-error status, and the specific message is lost. Throw an HttpError with statusCode 400 at this point.

verification.reason: The new check throws a plain Error inside the try. The catch only converts HttpError and Prisma errors to 400, so an empty dynamicUserList (for example `getUsernameList(undefined)`) becomes a 500 "Unable to load users".

findings.title: Prisma error messages are returned to the client as 400 responses
findings.body: The catch maps any PrismaClientKnownRequestError to `HttpError 400` with `error.message`, which can expose query or schema detail to the booker. Return a generic message for Prisma errors and keep the detail in the logs.

verification.reason: The catch passes the message of any PrismaClientKnownRequestError straight into a 400 HttpError returned to the client. That message can contain query or schema detail.

findings.title: Credentials loaded by id are not checked against the owner
findings.body: The new fallbacks in createAllCalendarEvents (lines 344-355) and updateAllCalendarEvents (lines 517-528) load a credential by id alone and then use it to write to an external calendar. The same pattern appears in handleCancelBooking.ts:433-437. The ids come from team destination calendars and booking references, which the system writes, so this is only a risk if that data is inconsistent. Is it intended that a reference id may resolve to a credential outside the booking's user or team?

verification.reason: Both new EventManager fallbacks load a credential by id with `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` and no userId or teamId check, then use it to write to an external calendar. The ids come from system-written destination calendars and references, so this is only a defensive question.

findings.title: Unrelated spelling change to user-visible calendar note
findings.body: The text changed from "organiser" to "organizer". This string is written into the calendar event notes, so the change is user-visible. It is not mentioned in the PR and does not relate to the multi-destination work. Split it into its own change, or mention it in the description.

verification.reason: The hidden-notes string changed from "organiser" to "organizer". It is written into calendar event notes, so users will see it. The change is unrelated to the multi-destination work.

contracts.action: Booking creation writes the event to each destination calendar (loop over destinationCalendar)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous single-destination branch in the same function (`createEvent(credential, event)` by destination.credentialId, or filter by integration)
contracts.before_after: Before: one destination, the calendar credential matched by credentialId, or all credentials of the integration type. After: every destination in the array. Destinations with a credentialId go to the matching credential, with a DB fallback. Destinations without one call createEvent for every credential of that type with no externalId.
contracts.visible_effect: The event appears on the chosen calendar of each host. Legacy destinations land in the primary calendar (Google), or duplicate events for the organizer on collective events.
contracts.failure_mode: The Google service ignores the externalId it is passed, so legacy destinations go to primary. A DB-miss credential is skipped with no log. Duplicates are possible (see EventManager finding). The Meet fallback can throw before any calendar is written (EventManager.ts:119).
contracts.open_question: Does the caller that builds EventManager pass only the organizer's credentials? That decides whether the else-branch duplication happens.

contracts.action: Cancel booking deletes calendar events from each booking reference
contracts.equivalent_path: Same file, same loop: `calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` (lines 470 and 480)
contracts.before_after: Before: one reference, credential from user.credentials. After: every calendar reference. A credential not in user.credentials is loaded from the DB by id. The deleteEvent call itself is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: The booking's calendar event is removed from the organizer's calendar. If the delete fails, the event stays visible on the calendar.
contracts.failure_mode: When the reference has no externalCalendarId, Google's deleteEvent now uses "primary" (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:317, 322). A 404 resolves silently (line 335). The cancelled event stays on the selected calendar with no error shown.

contracts.action: Google updateEvent (reschedule / location edit) picks the target calendar
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` in the same method
contracts.before_after: Before: falls back to the destination externalId when externalCalendarId is absent. After: the fallback is a self-comparison and yields undefined.
contracts.visible_effect: An update to a reference without externalCalendarId fails, so the event's time or location is not changed on the calendar.
contracts.failure_mode: Google rejects the update with calendarId undefined. CalendarManager.updateEvent logs it (CalendarManager.ts:299) and sets success false. The user sees no error.

contracts.equivalent_path: The previous expression in the same handler: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`
contracts.before_after: Before: slug stored when billing is disabled. After: slug stored only when billing is enabled.
contracts.visible_effect: On self-hosted deployments the new organization has no slug, so its URLs do not resolve.
contracts.failure_mode: The org is created without a slug and nothing reports the problem.

contracts.action: Load bookable users for a new booking (loadUsers)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous ternary in the same function (dynamic users via findMany, hosts, or eventType.users)
contracts.before_after: Before: an empty dynamicUserList returned no users. After: an empty or non-array list throws a plain Error, which becomes a 500. Prisma errors become a 400 with the Prisma message.
contracts.visible_effect: A client sending a bad dynamicUserList gets a 500 with "Unable to load users" instead of a 400.
contracts.failure_mode: The intended 400 is never produced. The error message is lost.

summary: Reviewed the 22 files in this part. The bulk were read from their diff hunks plus the surrounding code. I read EventManager.ts, CalendarManager.ts, the Google CalendarService.ts and create.handler.ts in more depth, and checked the Office365 service and the callers of Calendar.createEvent. I did not read every large file (handleNewBooking.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts) in full, so the findings are limited to the hunks and the code I did read. Main problems: an inverted org-slug condition unrelated to the PR; a TypeError in the Meet fallback when there is no destination calendar; the Google delete/update fallback compares a value to itself and yields undefined, so a cancelled event can stay on the user's calendar; legacy destinations are routed to "primary" on Google and ignore the user's chosen calendar; Office365 and Lark always use the first destination regardless of credential; a possible duplicate-create for collective events with legacy destinations; and a 400 that is returned as a 500 in loadUsers. Nothing was built or run.
